title: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 09 (Grand Annual Simulator IV (Section A 20 Marks))
subject: english-12

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly demonstrates the vocabulary word 'disabuse' in the context of student counseling?

options.A: The dean had to disabuse the father of the mistaken notion that his son was born to be an engineer.
options.B: The student disabused his books with highlighter markers.
options.C: The professor disabused the classroom before the lecture.
options.D: The doctor disabused medicine into the syringe.

questions.explanation: 'Disabuse' means to persuade someone that an idea or belief is mistaken or untrue.

questions.question: In Hawkes' essay, the expression 'to cultivate a habit of work' implies:

options.A: Growing agricultural plants in the university greenhouse
options.B: Systematically training oneself in regular, disciplined intellectual labor
options.C: Working as an apprentice in a machinery workshop
options.D: Doing all homework ten minutes before class

questions.explanation: 'Cultivating a habit of work' means disciplining the mind to sit down, focus, and complete academic tasks steadily every single day.

questions.question: In 'On Destroying Books', Squire names several types of books that clutter homes, including:

options.A: Inferior poetry volumes, outdated reference manuals, and worthless ephemeral novels

questions.explanation: Squire refers to bad minor poetry, tenth-rate novels, and useless pamphlets that consume shelf space.

questions.question: Which essayist wrote 'End of Term'?
questions.explanation: David Daiches, the renowned Scottish literary critic and historian, penned the autobiographical essay 'End of Term'.

questions.question: What does the demographic term 'infant mortality rate' measure?

options.A: The number of babies born in private hospitals
options.B: The number of deaths of infants under one year old per 1,000 live births in a given year
options.C: The percentage of children attending primary school
options.D: The number of pediatricians per city

questions.explanation: Infant mortality is a primary barometer of public health, measuring baby deaths per thousand live births.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'opulence' as contrasted with Chinese austerity?
questions.explanation: 'Opulence' signifies great wealth, luxury, and lavishness; its antonym is frugality, simplicity, or poverty.

questions.question: What was the psychological impact of the endless Saharan horizon on Christopher?

options.A: An acute feeling of insignificance and vulnerability under an immense, merciless sky
options.D: A feeling that he was in New York City

questions.explanation: The boundless, featureless sands create a profound sensation of human frailty against the colossal forces of nature.

questions.question: What key virtue unites Churchill at Harrow and Christopher in the Sahara?

options.A: Indomitable courage, perseverance, and resilience in the face of daunting adversity

questions.explanation: Both essays showcase indomitable perseverance—Churchill overcoming academic stigma and Christopher conquering the deadly Sahara.

questions.question: In what year did Fleming discover the penicillin mould contamination on his culture plate?
questions.explanation: Fleming discovered penicillin in September 1928 at St. Mary's Hospital, London.

questions.question: In Patrick Pringle's biographical essay on Sir Alexander Fleming, what major flaw of chemical antiseptics (like carbolic acid) during WW1 is highlighted?

options.A: They were too expensive to manufacture in wartime.
options.B: They destroyed the body's natural defense cells (leucocytes / white blood cells) more effectively than they killed the invading bacteria.
options.C: They had an unpleasant smell that caused headaches.
options.D: They caused immediate chemical fires in field hospitals.

questions.explanation: Sir Almroth Wright and Fleming proved that chemical antiseptics did more harm than good in deep wounds by killing leucocytes while bacteria survived deep in tissues.

questions.question: What monumental mausoleum in Ankara stands today as the national monument to Atatürk's legacy?
questions.explanation: Anıtkabir is the grand mausoleum in Ankara where millions of citizens and visiting world leaders pay homage to Atatürk.

questions.question: What official post was Mustafa Kemal appointed to by the Sultan's government in May 1919?

options.B: Inspector-General of the 9th (later 3rd) Army in Anatolia, tasked with disbanding Turkish rebel divisions
options.C: Minister of Foreign Affairs in Istanbul
options.D: Grand Admiral of the Ottoman Navy

questions.explanation: The Sultan sent Kemal to Anatolia to disarm patriotic guerrilla bands, but Kemal instead organized a nationwide resistance movement.

questions.question: How did Katherine view the strict class barriers of late Victorian England?

options.A: She believed they were artificial and ought to be dismantled through human sympathy, education, and social brotherhood.
options.B: She wanted only aristocrats to have rights.

questions.explanation: Her socialist and humanitarian ideals rejected snobbery, leading her to initiate the groundbreaking visit of East End London boys to Brookfield.

questions.question: What memorable piece of advice did venerable Headmaster Mr. Wetherby give young Chips on his first day in 1870?

options.A: 'Punish every boy with the cane on the first offence.'
options.B: 'Give your enthusiasm to Brookfield, and Brookfield will give you something in return. Take a firm attitude from the beginning with the boys.'

questions.explanation: Wetherby advised him to be firm from the start, as schoolboys are like wild colts who sense hesitation and pounce on weakness.

questions.question: What did Dr. Merivale say was the real secret to Chips' longevity?

options.A: An extraordinarily healthy constitution, lack of stress, and a peaceful heart untainted by malice or ambition

questions.explanation: A clean conscience, gentle lifestyle, and tranquil spirit gave Chips exceptional vitality into his eighties.

questions.question: Following Katherine's death, what noticeable change occurred in Chips' outward appearance and status at Brookfield?

options.A: He aged rapidly, grew prematurely grey, and became the revered 'Grand Old Man' and Senior Master of the school.
options.B: He became extremely aggressive and cruel.
options.C: He resigned and moved to Paris.
options.D: He dyed his hair and bought flashy sports cars.

questions.explanation: His hair turned white, his dry humor acquired a gentle philosophical depth, and he became the living soul of Brookfield.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'ephemeral' as used by Chips during the air raid ('these modern affairs are mere ephemera')?
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time; its opposite is enduring, permanent, or eternal.

questions.question: Whose name did Chips bravely read aloud in chapel among the war dead, despite fierce wartime anti-German hysteria?

options.A: Max Staefel, the former German master who had taught at Brookfield and was killed fighting on the Western Front

questions.explanation: Chips demonstrated supreme Christian humanity by honoring Max Staefel, a gentle former colleague who died fighting on the German side.

questions.question: Choose the correctly constructed sentence:

options.A: He ran as fastly as he could.
options.B: He ran as fast as he could.
options.C: He ran more fastly than anyone.
options.D: He ran as faster as possible.

questions.explanation: 'Fast' is both an adjective and an adverb; the word 'fastly' does not exist in standard English.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence regarding uncountable nouns:

options.A: The professor gave me many useful advices.
options.B: The professor gave me many useful pieces of advice.
options.C: The professor gave me an advice.

questions.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun with no plural 'advices'; pluralization requires a partitive counter ('pieces of advice').
